description:
Position Overview

The Natural History Museum at the University of Oslo is hiring a PhD Research Fellow to work on the diversity and ecology of marine algae and their protistan parasites. This is an employed doctoral position in the Norwegian style - a salaried job with full social benefits rather than a scholarship - based at Sars' gate 1 in Oslo. The fellow joins a strong interdisciplinary setting built around the museum, the Arctic Ocean 2050 initiative and the BIOCORE environment.

The scientific core of the project sits where metabarcoding meets marine ecology: using molecular tools to map which microalgae occur where, and how their protistan parasites shape those communities. It suits a candidate who is comfortable combining laboratory molecular work with computational analysis of biodiversity data.

Terms of Employment

Salary and benefits
ComponentDetails
SalaryNOK 550,800 - 595,000 per year depending on competence and experience (doctoral research fellow, position code 1017).
Deductions2% deducted for statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund (SPK).
PensionMembership of Statens Pensjonskasse, one of Norway's best public pension schemes, with favourable mortgage and insurance arrangements.
EnvironmentStructured onboarding, tailored career guidance and good welfare schemes.

Eligibility

Requirements
CriterionRequirement
DegreeMSc (or equivalent) in metabarcoding, microbiology, biodiversity, bioinformatics, ecology or a related field.
SkillsStrength in molecular biodiversity methods and/or bioinformatics; interest in marine protist ecology.
LocationPosition based in Oslo (Sars' gate 1, 0562 Oslo).

Application Dates

Key dates
ComponentDetails
StatusOpen when checked on 22 October 2026
Deadline4 November 2026
StartTo be agreed with the host department

How to Apply

Applications go through the official Jobbnorge listing - the apply button on this page. Norwegian doctoral adverts typically ask for a CV, transcripts, a short motivation statement and contact details for references through the portal, so have those files ready in the formats the portal requests. Applications sent by email are not considered.

About the Host

The University of Oslo is Norway's oldest and largest university, and its Natural History Museum runs nationally significant research collections and molecular facilities. Doctoral researchers there are full employees, and the museum's marine and protist groups collaborate widely across the Nordic research infrastructure.
